title: Bresenham's line algorithm
instructions:
## Pixels are integers

A line from (x0, y0) to (x1, y1) must be drawn with whole pixels. Bresenham's algorithm picks them with integer arithmetic only.

## Do this

Write `bresenham(x0, y0, x1, y1)` returning the list of `[x, y]` pixels from the start point to the end point inclusive, for **any** direction (use the general form with `dx`, `dy`, `sx`, `sy` and the error term). Then `rasterise(points, width, height)` returning an array of strings, one per row, with `#` for set pixels and `.` elsewhere (row 0 at the top).
hints: const dx = Math.abs(x1 - x0), sx = x0 < x1 ? 1 : -1, dy = -Math.abs(y1 - y0), sy = y0 < y1 ? 1 : -1; let err = dx + dy;
Loop: push [x0, y0]; if (x0 === x1 && y0 === y1) break; const e2 = 2 * err; if (e2 >= dy) { err += dy; x0 += sx; } if (e2 <= dx) { err += dx; y0 += sy; }
For rasterise, start with rows of width "." and replace the character at x in row y.

checks.label: bresenham chooses the right pixels in every octant
checks.name: bresenham

realityNote: GPUs rasterise lines and triangle edges with the same incremental idea, in hardware, millions of times a frame. Anti-aliased lines (Wu) trade the integer purity for a second pixel with partial coverage.
